title: Chaotic intervals
author: isajo4002
rules:
This was a collaboration with I Love Sleeping and was made as an homage to qodec whos catalog I recently finished and introduced me to interval sums which I haven't seen anywhere else so I wanted to explore it a bit more

Normal chaos construction rules apply:

Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column, and 9 cell region.

Regions must be discovered by the solver and every region is orthogonally connected.

Interval Sums:

A and B are the two cells nearest an outside clue in the row or column indicated by that clue and the outside clue represents the sum of the digits in positions A through B, counted from that outside clue away into the grid.

A ? can be an positive number.

Position A and B are in two different regions and every cell in between them if there are any are in a third region.

Here is an example of how the regions work with a link to the solvable puzzle
